risk_summary.high: Do not click any link, and do not send any details or money.
risk_summary.medium: Slow down and check the sender through their official channel before doing anything.
risk_summary.low: This does not mean the message is certainly safe. Always check the official channel.

reasons.deposit_to_reserve: It asks for a deposit before you see the flat or item, or says the owner is abroad. This is how rental and listing scams work.
reasons.transfer_only: It refuses cash on delivery and only takes an advance transfer, so you can't get your money back.
reasons.too_good_deal: A price or discount far below the market. Unreal offers are a common bait for fake shops.
reasons.charity_appeal: A request to donate by transfer or through a link. Donate only through licensed charities and their official channels.
reasons.personal_account: It asks for payment to a personal account. Real organisations are paid into accounts in their own name.
reasons.visa_offer: It promises a 'guaranteed' or fast visa or residency. Visas are only issued through official government channels.
reasons.romance_money: Affectionate words together with a request for money, tickets or fees. This is the classic romance scam.
reasons.romance_profile: An online relationship with someone never met in person, or a far-away job story (oil rig, military mission).
reasons.recovery_offer: It promises to recover money you lost. This is a second scam aimed at victims; police never charge to recover funds.
reasons.otp_request: It asks for a one-time code (OTP). Official bodies never ask for it.
reasons.card_details: It asks for bank card details.
reasons.account_suspended: It threatens to block your account or card to scare you.
reasons.gov_impersonation: It uses a government body's name or mentions a fine.
reasons.delivery: It talks about a parcel or delivery, a very common scam.
reasons.payment_request: It asks you to pay or transfer money.
reasons.small_amount: It asks for a small amount, a trick to steal your card details.
reasons.urgency: It rushes you so you do not stop to think.
reasons.prize: It promises a prize you never entered for.
reasons.job_offer: An easy job or unrealistic income.
reasons.upfront_fee: It asks for an upfront fee. Real employers do not.
reasons.investment: It talks about investment, trading or profits.
reasons.guaranteed: It promises guaranteed returns. No real investment does.
reasons.extortion_threat: A threat to publish photos, videos or chats. This is extortion, a crime.
reasons.secrecy: It asks you to tell no one.
reasons.remote_access: It asks you to install an app that lets someone control your device.
reasons.gift_cards: It asks for payment in gift cards, a scammer favourite.
reasons.crypto_payment: It asks for payment in crypto, which is hard to recover.
reasons.personal_info_request: It asks for personal details such as your ID or passport.
reasons.link_click: It asks you to click a link.
reasons.official_link: The link is on a known official domain.

url_flags.brand_lookalike: imitates a known brand but is not its official site
url_flags.risky_tld: a domain ending often used in scams
url_flags.shortener: a short link that hides the destination

general: Never share your one-time code or card details with anyone.
Check with the organisation on its official number, not the one in the message.
If it is a scam, report it to Aman on 8002626 or at ecrime.ae.
delivery_scam: Track parcels only in the courier's own app or official website.
bank_impersonation: Call your bank on the number printed on the back of your card.
gov_impersonation: Check fines and fees only in official government apps and websites.
otp_theft: A one-time code approves a transaction. Anyone asking for it wants to use your account.
job_scam: Real employers never charge you for a job or a visa.
investment_scam: Check that the platform is licensed by a financial regulator before investing.
prize_scam: Real prizes never ask you to pay a fee to claim them.
extortion: Do not pay or negotiate. Paying does not stop extortion.
Do not delete the chats. Keep screenshots as evidence.
Report to the police now. You are not alone, and reports are handled confidentially.
tech_support: Never install a remote-control app because a caller asked you to.
shopping_scam: Never pay a deposit before seeing the flat or item yourself, and check the owner's identity and a registered tenancy contract.
Shop at known stores, and prefer cash on delivery or a card that lets you dispute the charge.
charity_scam: Donate only through charities licensed in the UAE and their official apps and websites, never to personal accounts.
visa_scam: Check any visa or residency on official government websites and apps, and never pay an agent who promises it is guaranteed.
romance_scam: Never send money to someone you haven't met in person, however moving the story.
Ask for a live video call, and talk to someone you trust before deciding anything.
recovery_scam: Never pay a fee to get your money back. Follow up your case with the police directly: Aman 8002626 or ecrime.ae.
phishing_link: Type the official website address yourself instead of tapping the link.

money_sent.title: I paid, or shared my card details or a one-time code
steps: Call your bank now on the number on the back of your card. Ask them to block the card and stop the transaction.
Do not delete the messages, chats or call log.
Take screenshots: the message, the link, the sender's number and the debit alert.
Report to the police now: every minute makes recovery harder.
Change your banking app and e-mail passwords from a safe device.
Stop all contact with the scammer.

account_hacked.title: My account was hacked (WhatsApp, Instagram, e-mail...)
steps: Use 'Forgot password' or account recovery in the official app.
Turn on two-step verification as soon as you are back in.
Tell friends and family not to send money or codes to anyone using your name.
Check the devices logged in to the account and remove any you do not know.
If someone asks for money to return the account, do not pay. Report it.

extortion.title: Someone is threatening to publish my photos or chats
steps: You are not to blame. The person threatening you is committing the crime.
Do not pay: paying rarely ends it and often makes it worse.
Do not delete the chats. Screenshot the account and the threats.
Stop replying, and do not send any more photos or videos.
Report it to the police now. Reports are handled confidentially.
If you are under 18, tell a parent or an adult you trust.

harassment.title: I'm being bullied, harassed or insulted online
steps: Don't answer abuse with abuse: an insulting reply can count against you too.
Screenshot the account, the date and the abusive words, and don't delete them.
Block the account and use the app's own 'Report' option.
Online insults, defamation and harassment are crimes under UAE law. Report it to the police.
If you are under 18, tell a parent or a teacher you trust.
If there is a threat to hurt you, call 999.

impersonation.title: Someone made a fake account with my name or photo
steps: Screenshot the fake account, its link and its username.
Report it in the app as 'impersonation', and ask your friends to report it too.
Post from your real account that a fake one exists and that you never ask anyone for money or codes.
If the fake account asked anyone for money, report it to the police now.
Make your photos and friends list private, and turn on two-step verification.

privacy_violation.title: Someone filmed me, or posted my photos or personal details without permission
steps: Screenshot the post, its link, the account name and the date before it is deleted.
Ask for removal using the app's 'Report a privacy violation' option.
Don't share the content again yourself, even to warn people about it.
Filming people or posting their photos or details without permission is a crime under UAE law. Report it to the police.
If your address or numbers were posted and you feel unsafe, call 999.

device_hacked.title: My phone or computer is hacked, or my files are locked for a ransom
steps: Take the device offline now: turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data, and unplug the network cable.
Don't pay the ransom: paying doesn't guarantee your files back, and it funds the criminals.
If your phone suddenly loses signal and messages stop, call your telecom provider now: your SIM may have been moved to another device.
From another, safe device, change your e-mail and banking passwords and turn on two-step verification.
Photograph the ransom note or any strange message, and don't delete anything.
Report it to the police. If it is a work device, tell your company's IT team at once.

identity_shared.title: I sent my ID or passport to someone suspicious
steps: Report it to the police so it is on record that your documents may be misused.
Tell your bank and ask them to watch for new applications in your name.
Watch for any SIM card, account or loan opened in your name.
Keep a copy of the chat where you sent the document.

business_fraud.title: My business paid a fake invoice or a transfer asked for by the 'boss' or a 'supplier'
steps: Call the company's bank now and ask them to recall the transfer and freeze it at the receiving bank.
Call the supplier or manager on a number you already know, not the number or e-mail in the request.
Keep the full messages with e-mail addresses, the invoice and the transfer receipt.
Change the company e-mail passwords and turn on two-step verification: the mailbox may be hacked.
Report it to the police now: every hour lowers the chance of getting the money back.
Make it a rule: any change to a supplier's bank details is confirmed by a phone call.

suspicious_only.title: I got a suspicious message but did not respond
steps: Well done: do not tap the link and do not reply.
Block the number or account, and use 'Report spam' in the app.
Report it to the police to protect others from the same campaign.
Warn your family, especially older relatives.

contacts.aman: Aman service - Abu Dhabi Police (toll-free call)
contacts.child_protection_moi: Child Protection Centre - Ministry of Interior (and the Hemayati app)
contacts.child_protection_moe: Child Protection Unit - Ministry of Education

Hello, I'm Haris 🛡️
Forward me any suspicious message, or paste its text or link here, and I'll tell you how risky it is and what to do.

I don't keep your messages, and I hide your personal details before checking.

🔔 To get the authority's warnings about scam campaigns, send: ALERTS
whatsapp.footer: An AI assistant, not an official body · Emergency 999

whatsapp.next: What would you like to do now?
whatsapp.scammed_intro: Don't worry, we'll go step by step. Choose what happened:

playbooks.money_sent: I paid or gave a code
playbooks.identity_shared: I sent my ID or passport

whatsapp.report_app: To send a report to the authority now, tap "File a report".
whatsapp.guide:
Haris in three steps:
1. *Check before you reply:* forward me the suspicious message and I'll tell you the risk, why, and what to do.
2. *Something went wrong?* Tap "I've been scammed" and choose your case for the first steps and the official reporting numbers.
3. *Protect others:* if it was a scam and you didn't reply, tap "Report to protect".
whatsapp.reported:
Thank you, your report was received 🙏
Every report helps spot a campaign early, and the authority decides on any official warning.

visitor.title: Visiting the UAE?
tips: Card from a bank abroad? Call the international number on the back and ask them to block it now.
Passport lost, stolen, or a photo of it sent to a suspicious party? Tell the police, then your embassy.
Keep the report number and file for your travel insurance and your bank at home.
You don't need an Emirates ID: you can report with your passport, and the Tourism Police follows your case even after you leave the UAE.

child.title: Under 18?
tips: It is not your fault: the person threatening or hurting you is. Tell a parent or an adult you trust, such as a school counsellor.
Don't send any more photos, and never attach a private photo of yourself to a report: screenshot only the person's account and messages.
The Child Protection Centre helps you in confidence on 116111 or in the Hemayati app, even if you can't tell your family.
